benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, triangulated from MLIT transaction data via Utinokati (multi-year, standardised) and 2026 official residential land-price points via Totinokati/tochidai: Matsudo ~70 (official residential average on 14 points; the all-use station average of ~132 mixes station-front commercial plots — Honcho alone is ~422 — and is not used, and quarterly transaction prints swing from 54 to 115 on 5–7 deals), Shin-Matsudo ~64, Kamihongo ~60 (official points thin at 3, corroborated by its house catchment), Minoridai ~58, Kita-Matsudo ~55, Mabashi ~52, Kita-Kogane ~48 (transaction regression 47.8, official 42.5 and all-use 46.9 converge), Matsudo-Shinden ~46, Goko ~44, Mutsumi/Rokujitsu ~34. Higashi-Matsudo is scored at ~60, NOT Utinokati's ~40 regression: that figure is dragged down by urbanisation-control (調整区域) deals in Kamishiki trading at 3–16万円/坪 on 270–1,000m² lots, which are not residential comparables. Yabashira/Shin-Yahashira (~55) and Koganehara (~43, a district with no station of its own, bus to Kita-Kogane) are proxies from official district points and neighbouring-station transactions, flagged as such. Yakiri (~53) rests on an all-use district print only — low confidence; Motoyama (~44), Akiyama (~57) and Koganejoshi (~56) appear in the house file only and rest on district-level prints, flagged as such. Walk bands use Matsudo's observed land gradient — prices fall roughly 30% by a 10-minute walk and 50% by 16+ minutes (city transactions: 85.4万円/坪 within 5 minutes vs 42.8 at 16+); house prices fall only ~12% over the same range. Used houses transacted at about ¥107万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis): Matsudo station catchment ~132, Shin-Matsudo ~123, Kamihongo ~129 at the top; by age, ≤10-yr stock ~139 falls to ~65 for 30+-yr stock. The district print of ~362 for Nemoto rests on a handful of non-standard deals and is ignored. Official residential land prices rose +8.0% in the 2026 公示地価 survey (+8.9% in 基準地価, the Tokyo belt's second-fastest rise) — the fourth straight year of acceleration (+2.3% in 2023 to +8.0% in 2026).
